messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty -> SEV2: Multiple customer egress failures in eu-west-1. Paging oncall-sre.
mike (oncall-sre): acknowledged, on pager. I'm seeing a jump in nat_gateway.5xx_errors and lots of TCP RSTs from hosts in eu-west-1b.
sarah (netops): any RouteTable changes today? I noticed a terraform apply that touched rtb-0a1b2c3d earlier.
deepak (eng-runtime): support is reporting webhook delivery failures and retry storms. sample curl just hangs at SYN then times out.
mike (oncall-sre): grabbing VPC flow logs for 10.1.42.78 -> 0.0.0.0/0 to see path.
mike (oncall-sre): flow log snippet: src=10.1.42.78 dst=35.201.12.8 action=REJECT rule=NACL-1001-OUTBOUND. Looks like return traffic being dropped.
jen (support): customers A and B started seeing 502/timeout errors around 06:12 UTC. Ticket volume spiked.
sarah (netops): scanning routing: rtb-0a1b2c3d has 0.0.0.0/0 -> eni-09f8e7d6. That ENI is in the staging VPC. Huh. Tag-based selector might have picked the wrong ENI.
deepak (eng-runtime): confirmed: new infra module created ephemeral egress ENIs for NAT warm-up. Tag key used was "egress-role:nat-eni" and staging happened to use same tag. Selection logic didn't constrain by vpc-id.
mike (oncall-sre): so route points to an ENI in another VPC causing asymmetric routing, return packets get lost and NAT gateway metrics show errors.
sarah (netops): immediate plan: replace route to point at nat-0a1b2c3d (the correct NAT gateway), and add a fallback route to a known NAT instance while we audit. Executing emergency replace now.

```
# emergency route update
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0a1b2c3d --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --nat-gateway-id nat-0a1b2c3d
```

sarah (netops): route replace succeeded. please validate egress from affected hosts.
mike (oncall-sre): running quick curl from 10.1.42.78 -> external endpoint. Getting HTTP 200, latency ~120ms. Progressing.
jen (support): customers reporting improvements. Backlog draining but a few retries still failing (DNS cache pointing to wrong egress IP).
deepak (eng-runtime): partner clients cached the old public IP (from the wrong ENI). TTL was 3600s. We'll hasten DNS changes.
sarah (netops): lowering TTL and upserting correct A record in Route53 to speed propagation. Submitting change batch.

```
# route53 change batch
{
  "Changes": [
    {"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"egress.redwood-eu.example.com","Type":"A","TTL":60,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"3.120.45.10"}]}}
  ]
}
```

sarah (netops): change submitted (chg-IX12345) status=PENDING.
mike (oncall-sre): while DNS propagates, I'll open the NACL to allow ephemeral return ports so asymmetric drops are reduced.

```
# emergency NACL tweak
# before: outbound ephemeral ports denied
# after: allow TCP 1024-65535 outbound to 0.0.0.0/0
```

sarah (netops): updated nacl-0b2c3d4e outbound rule 100 to allow TCP ports 1024-65535 to 0.0.0.0/0.
jen (support): error rate dropped from ~8% to ~0.7% in last 10m; many customers seeing successful deliveries now.
mike (oncall-sre): provisioning a small t3.small NAT instance in a public subnet with squid as a deterministic egress IP for any remaining misrouted routes. Boot script applied.
sarah (netops): opening a revert PR for the Terraform module that introduced ENI selection by tag. Will mark for expeditious apply in eu-west-1.
deepak (eng-runtime): post-incident note: module allowed selection by a non-unique tag. We should validate uniqueness and VPC constraint in plan to avoid cross-VPC selection.
mike (oncall-sre): metrics: nat gateway errors back to baseline after route replacement and NACL update. Route53 now showing propagation in our checks but change still PENDING for global caches.
incident-bot: Incident SRE-2026-03-15-1798765432 status -> Mitigated (Partial impact).
jen (support): drafting customer notification: "Intermittent outbound failures in eu-west-1 due to route pointing to ENI in wrong VPC. We replaced route, opened NACL, and spun up a temporary NAT instance. Some partners may see retries until DNS caches expire (TTL lowered). No data loss. Postmortem forthcoming."
mike (oncall-sre): agree. Will update channel when Route53 reaches INSYNC.
sarah (netops): Route53 change IN_SYNC now. Reverting Terraform change and adding a precondition so ENI selection filters by vpc-id. Applying revert.

```
# terraform validation snippet
data "aws_network_interface" "selected" {
  filter { name = "tag:egress-role" , values = ["nat-eni"] }
  filter { name = "vpc-id" , values = [var.vpc_id] }
}
```

deepak (eng-runtime): I'll own the follow-up ticket: add plan-time validation, test coverage for tag uniqueness, and update infra playbook with emergency egress steps.
mike (oncall-sre): handing off to sarah for post-incident ownership. My oncall ends in ~30m.

--- HANDOFF ---
sarah (netops): taking ownership for postmortem and remediation. Action items: 1) revert tf module + add precondition 2) tests for unique tag selection 3) update runbook: dns-ttl lowering + nacl emergency script 4) finalize customer comms and attach logs.
mike (oncall-sre): concise RCA for postmortem: cause = ambiguous ENI selection via non-unique tag -> route to wrong ENI -> asymmetric return path + NACL deny -> outbound webhook failures. Mitigation = route replace to NAT gateway, temporary NACL relax, temp NAT instance, lower DNS TTL, and revert terraform. Impact = partial outage for outbound integrations in eu-west-1 from ~06:12 UTC, mitigated by ~06:46 UTC. Pages escalated to SEV2.
jen (support): attaching customer logs and timestamps to the incident ticket.
incident-bot: Incident SRE-2026-03-15-1798765432 updated: Status -> Postmortem Required. Assigned -> sarah.
sarah (netops): scheduling a postmortem meeting for 48h. Will post RCA and remediation plan in the incident ticket. :thumbsup:
